board_events.text: Rule 1: S PHASE doubles the DNA but NOT the chromosome number.
Rule 2: MEIOSIS I halves the chromosome number.
Rule 3: MEIOSIS II separates the chromatids, halving the DNA again.
Do not memorise six rows. Memorise three rules and REBUILD the rows.
Notice each rule touches a DIFFERENT combination of the three columns.
The end product of meiosis — a gamete — has HALF the chromosomes AND HALF the DNA of the diploid parent.

segments.text: <excited>Now the compression, and this is the most valuable thirty seconds in the part. Those six rows across two tables are not six facts. They are three rules.
Three boxes. And under each one, exactly what it changes and exactly what it leaves alone.

Rule one. S phase doubles the D N A but not the chromosome number. Two C to four C, while two n stays two n. This is the trap we opened part one with, and it is still the highest yield sentence in the chapter.
Rule two. Meiosis one halves the chromosome number. Two n to n, while the chromatids stay at two. Reductional, because homologues separate.
Rule three. Meiosis two separates the chromatids, halving the D N A again. Two C to one C, while n stays n. Equational, because chromatids separate.
So do not memorise six rows. Memorise three rules and rebuild the rows when you need them. Six rows is a burden; three rules is a tool. And a tool works on questions you have not seen before.

And notice why three rules suffice. Each one touches a different combination of the three columns. S phase, D N A only. Meiosis one, number and D N A. Meiosis two, chromatids and D N A. No two rules do the same thing, so no rule is redundant.

And the conclusion the three rules deliver. The end product of meiosis, a gamete, has half the chromosomes and half the D N A of the diploid parent. Both. Not just the number. That is the sentence to write when a question asks what a gamete carries.
<excited>अब compression, और ये इस part के सबसे क़ीमती तीस सेकंड हैं। दोनों tables की वो छह rows, छह facts नहीं हैं। वो तीन rules हैं।
तीन boxes. और हर एक के नीचे, वो क्या बदलता है और क्या छोड़ देता है, बिल्कुल साफ़।

पहला नियम. S phase D N A को double करता है पर chromosome number को नहीं। Two C से four C, जबकि two n, two n ही रहता है। यही वो trap है जिससे हमने part one खोला था, और ये अब भी chapter का सबसे highest yield वाक्य है।
दूसरा नियम. Meiosis one chromosome number को आधा करता है। Two n से n, जबकि chromatids दो ही रहते हैं। Reductional, क्योंकि homologues separate होते हैं।
तीसरा नियम. Meiosis two chromatids को अलग करता है, और D N A को दोबारा आधा कर देता है। Two C से one C, जबकि n, n ही रहता है। Equational, क्योंकि chromatids separate होते हैं।
तो छह rows मत रटिए। तीन rules याद कीजिए और ज़रूरत पड़ने पर rows दोबारा बना लीजिए। छह rows एक बोझ हैं; तीन rules एक औज़ार। और औज़ार उन सवालों पर भी चलता है जो आपने पहले नहीं देखे।

और ग़ौर कीजिए तीन rules क्यों काफ़ी हैं। हर एक तीन columns के अलग combination को छूता है। S phase, सिर्फ़ D N A. Meiosis one, number और D N A. Meiosis two, chromatids और D N A. कोई दो rules एक ही काम नहीं करते, तो कोई भी redundant नहीं।

और तीनों rules जो नतीजा देते हैं वो ये। Meiosis का अंतिम उत्पाद, यानी gamete, में diploid parent के आधे chromosomes और आधी D N A होती है। दोनों। सिर्फ़ number नहीं। जब सवाल पूछे gamete क्या लेकर चलता है, यही वाक्य लिखिए।

board_events.text: (a) Pairing of homologues (synapsis) and chiasmata occur ONLY in meiosis. So this is MEIOSIS.
(b) Chiasmata first become clearly visible in DIPLOTENE of Prophase I (Meiosis I).
(c) NO. Synapsis requires homologous PAIRS, which exist only in a diploid cell. So the cell must be DIPLOID.
One observed structure forces a conclusion about the whole cell. That is what 'integrative' means.

segments.text: Now two integrative examples that span the whole chapter. The first is an identify from clues item, and it is a lovely piece of question design — two observations, three conclusions.
In a dividing cell, homologous chromosomes are seen paired, and a chiasma is visible between them. That is all you are given. Two observations.
Three questions. A, is this mitosis or meiosis? B, name the division and the exact stage. C, could this cell be haploid?
The observation on the left, the three answers on the right, and the reasoning chain for part c along the bottom.

Part a. Pairing of homologues — synapsis — and chiasmata occur only in meiosis. So this is meiosis, not mitosis. And this is exactly the only in meiosis row of the master table paying off. The question told you the answer in its own wording.

Part b. Chiasmata first become clearly visible in diplotene of prophase one, which is in Meiosis one. Note the precision demanded — the division is Meiosis one, and the exact stage is diplotene. Not pachytene, where the crossing over actually happened.
Part c, and this is the part that separates candidates. No — the cell cannot be haploid. Synapsis requires homologous pairs, and pairs exist only in a diploid cell. So the cell must be diploid.

And notice what just happened. One observed structure — a chiasma — forced a conclusion about the ploidy of the entire cell. That is what integrative means. You did not recall a fact about haploidy; you derived it from what you could see.
अब दो integrative examples जो पूरे chapter को समेटते हैं। पहला identify from clues वाला item है, और ये question design का एक ख़ूबसूरत नमूना है — दो observations, तीन नतीजे।
एक divide होते cell में, homologous chromosomes paired दिखते हैं, और उनके बीच एक chiasma दिखता है। बस इतना ही दिया है। दो observations.
तीन सवाल। A, ये mitosis है या meiosis? B, division और exact stage का नाम बताइए। C, क्या ये cell haploid हो सकता है?
बाईं तरफ़ observation, दाईं तरफ़ तीनों जवाब, और सबसे नीचे part c की reasoning chain.

Part a. Homologues का pairing — synapsis — और chiasmata सिर्फ़ meiosis में होते हैं। तो ये meiosis है, mitosis नहीं। और यही master table की only in meiosis वाली row का फल है। सवाल ने अपने ही शब्दों में जवाब दे दिया।

Part b. Chiasmata पहली बार साफ़ diplotene में दिखते हैं, जो prophase one में है, यानी Meiosis one में। ग़ौर कीजिए कितनी precision माँगी गई — division है Meiosis one, और exact stage है diplotene. Pachytene नहीं, जहाँ crossing over असल में हुआ था।
Part c, और यही हिस्सा उम्मीदवारों को अलग करता है। नहीं — ये cell haploid नहीं हो सकता। Synapsis को homologous pairs चाहिए, और pairs सिर्फ़ diploid cell में होते हैं। तो cell को diploid होना ही होगा।

और ग़ौर कीजिए अभी क्या हुआ। एक दिखी हुई structure — एक chiasma — ने पूरे cell की ploidy के बारे में नतीजा थोप दिया। Integrative का मतलब यही है। आपने haploidy का कोई fact याद नहीं किया; आपने उसे जो दिख रहा था उससे derive किया।

board_events.text: (a) One meiosis $\to$ 4 haploid cells. Chromosome number $= n = 16 \div 2 = 8$ each.
(b) If its DNA in G2 is 8C, what is the DNA per pollen grain?
After TWO divisions the DNA is reduced to ONE-QUARTER of the G2 value: $8C \div 4 = 2C$.
Note the labels are relative: 2C here is the HAPLOID amount, because this cell's unreplicated diploid value is 4C.

segments.text: The second integrative example is a three part numerical, and it exercises all three columns of our bookkeeping at once.
A pollen mother cell of a plant with two n equals sixteen undergoes meiosis. Note the words pollen mother cell — that tells you it is a meiocyte, and it licenses the one to four ratio.
Part a. How many pollen grains are formed, and what is their chromosome number? Two quantities asked, so give two.
The figure works both parts. One meiocyte to four grains along the top, and the D N A chain along the bottom.
Part a. One meiosis gives four haploid cells, so four pollen grains. And their chromosome number is n, which is sixteen divided by two, so eight each. Four grains, eight chromosomes apiece.
Part b. If its D N A in G two is eight C, what is the D N A per pollen grain? Now we are on the third column, and the chromosome answer from part a does not help us here.
Apply rule three, twice. After two divisions the D N A is reduced to one quarter of the G two value. Eight C divided by four is two C. So each pollen grain has two C worth of D N A.

One point of care, because the labels can look contradictory. Two C here is the haploid amount, because this particular cell's unreplicated diploid value is four C, not two C. The C labels are relative to whatever baseline the question sets. It is consistent either way — a quarter of G two is the answer regardless of what you call it.
दूसरा integrative example तीन हिस्सों वाला numerical है, और ये हमारी bookkeeping के तीनों columns को एक साथ चलाता है।

एक plant का pollen mother cell, जिसका two n बराबर sixteen है, meiosis से गुज़रता है। Pollen mother cell शब्दों पर ग़ौर कीजिए — वो बता देते हैं कि ये meiocyte है, और one to four ratio की इजाज़त दे देते हैं।
Part a. कितने pollen grains बनते हैं, और उनका chromosome number क्या है? दो quantities पूछी हैं, तो दो दीजिए।
Figure दोनों हिस्से हल करता है। ऊपर एक meiocyte से चार grains, और नीचे D N A की कड़ी।
Part a. एक meiosis चार haploid cells देता है, तो चार pollen grains. और उनका chromosome number है n, यानी sixteen divided by two, तो हर एक में eight. चार grains, हर एक में eight chromosomes.
Part b. अगर G two में उसका D N A eight C है, तो हर pollen grain में कितना D N A? अब हम तीसरे column पर हैं, और part a का chromosome वाला जवाब यहाँ काम नहीं आता।
तीसरा नियम दो बार लगाइए। दो divisions के बाद D N A, G two की value का एक चौथाई रह जाता है। Eight C divided by four यानी two C. तो हर pollen grain में two C जितना D N A है।

एक सावधानी, क्योंकि labels विरोधाभासी लग सकते हैं। यहाँ two C haploid amount है, क्योंकि इस ख़ास cell की unreplicated diploid value four C है, two C नहीं। C labels उस baseline के हिसाब से हैं जो सवाल तय करता है। दोनों तरह से बात एक ही है — जवाब G two का एक चौथाई है, चाहे आप उसे कुछ भी कहें।

board_events.text: Anchor: one meiosis $\to$ 4 haploid cells.
$240 \div 4 = 60$ meiocytes.
General rule: meiocytes needed = cells required $\div$ 4.
Do NOT reach for the mitotic rule here. Mitosis compounds as $2^n$; meiosis is a one-off giving exactly 4.
Ask which process the question describes BEFORE you pick a formula.
Notice this one question used all three columns: chromosome number in (a), DNA in (b), cell count in (c).

segments.text: Part c of the same question, and it is the one you should be able to answer in about three seconds.
How many such meiocytes are needed to make two hundred and forty pollen grains?
The anchor on the left, the sum in the middle, the general rule underneath, and in red the rule you must not reach for.
State the anchor before the arithmetic. One meiosis gives four haploid cells. That is the entire content of the question — everything else is division.
Two hundred and forty divided by four is sixty. Sixty meiocytes. One line.
And generalise it into the rule you carry. Meiocytes needed equals cells required divided by four. That covers every question of this shape you will meet.

And the warning, because you now know two counting rules and they are easy to confuse. Do not reach for the mitotic rule here. Mitosis repeats and compounds as two to the power n. Meiosis is a fixed one off that gives exactly four. Different process, different rule.

So the habit is to ask which process the question describes before you pick a formula. If it says a cell divides repeatedly, that is mitosis and you want two to the power n. If it says a meiocyte undergoes meiosis, you want divide by four. Read the verb.

And notice what this one question just did. Part a used the chromosome number column. Part b used the D N A column. Part c used the cell count. Three parts, three different quantities — which is exactly why we set up three columns and never merged them.
उसी सवाल का part c, और यही वो है जिसका जवाब आपको लगभग तीन सेकंड में देना चाहिए।
Two hundred and forty pollen grains बनाने के लिए ऐसे कितने meiocytes चाहिए?
बाईं तरफ़ anchor, बीच में सवाल, नीचे general rule, और लाल में वो नियम जिस पर हाथ नहीं बढ़ाना है।
Arithmetic से पहले anchor लिखिए। एक meiosis चार haploid cells देता है। यही सवाल का पूरा content है — बाक़ी सब भाग है।
Two hundred and forty divided by four यानी sixty. Sixty meiocytes. एक line.
और इसे उस rule में बदल लीजिए जो आप साथ रखेंगे। Meiocytes चाहिए बराबर cells required divided by four. इस shape का जो भी सवाल मिलेगा, ये उसे cover कर लेता है।

और चेतावनी, क्योंकि अब आपको दो counting rules आते हैं और उन्हें मिलाना आसान है। यहाँ mitotic rule पर हाथ मत बढ़ाइए। Mitosis दोहराता है और two to the power n की तरह compound होता है। Meiosis एक तय, एक-बारगी चीज़ है जो ठीक चार देता है। अलग process, अलग rule.

तो आदत ये है कि formula चुनने से पहले पूछिए सवाल किस process की बात कर रहा है। अगर वो कहे कोई cell बार-बार divide करता है, तो वो mitosis है और आपको two to the power n चाहिए। अगर कहे कोई meiocyte meiosis से गुज़रता है, तो चार से भाग चाहिए। Verb पढ़िए।

और ग़ौर कीजिए इस एक सवाल ने क्या किया। Part a ने chromosome number वाला column इस्तेमाल किया। Part b ने D N A वाला। Part c ने cell count. तीन हिस्से, तीन अलग quantities — और यही वजह है कि हमने तीन columns बनाए और उन्हें कभी मिलाया नहीं।

sections.title: Rapid revision I — the cell cycle and the mitotic stages

board_events.text: Rapid full-chapter revision: must-know one-liners
1. Cell cycle = Interphase ($\gt 95\%$, ~23 h in humans) + M phase (~1 h). Order: $G_1 \to S \to G_2 \to M$.
2. S phase: DNA doubles, chromosome number unchanged; the centriole duplicates (animal cells).
3. $G_0$: quiescent, OUT of the cycle; e.g. nerve and muscle cells.
4. Mitosis stages: PMAT — Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase.
5. Metaphase = chromosomes at the equatorial plate; the BEST stage to study chromosome morphology.
Careful: longest phase is INTERPHASE. Best stage to study chromosomes is METAPHASE. Two different questions.

segments.text: Now a rapid revision pass over the whole chapter, as one-liners. This is what you read the night before. Take them in three groups.
One. The cell cycle is interphase, more than ninety five percent of it, about twenty three hours in humans, plus M phase, about one hour. And the order is G one, S, G two, M.
Two, and it is the one to know cold. S phase — the D N A doubles, the chromosome number is unchanged. And the centriole duplicates, in animal cells. That last clause is a C U E T favourite.
Three. G zero is quiescent and it is out of the cycle — not a fourth phase inside it. Nerve and muscle cells are the standard examples. Cells exit to G zero from G one.
Four. The mitosis stages are P M A T. Prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase. Please make a two.

Five. Metaphase is chromosomes at the equatorial plate, and it is the best stage to study chromosome morphology. Remember the reason — most condensed and least overlapping, which is why karyotyping uses it.

And guard that pair, because the paper likes to put them next to each other. The longest phase is interphase. The best stage to study chromosomes is metaphase. Two different questions with two different answers, and length is not the criterion for the second one — resolvability is.
अब पूरे chapter पर एक rapid revision, one-liners की शक्ल में। यही आप imtihan से एक रात पहले पढ़ेंगे। इन्हें तीन groups में लीजिए।
एक. Cell cycle यानी interphase, जो उसका ninety five percent से ज़्यादा है, humans में लगभग twenty three hours, plus M phase, लगभग एक घंटा। और order है G one, S, G two, M.
दो, और यही पक्का याद होना चाहिए। S phase — D N A double होता है, chromosome number unchanged रहता है। और centriole duplicate होता है, animal cells में। ये आख़िरी हिस्सा C U E T का favourite है।
तीन. G zero quiescent है और cycle के बाहर है — उसके अंदर का चौथा phase नहीं। Nerve और muscle cells standard examples हैं। Cells, G one से G zero में निकलते हैं।
चार. Mitosis के stages हैं P M A T. Prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase. Please make a two.

पाँच. Metaphase यानी equatorial plate पर chromosomes, और chromosome morphology study करने के लिए यही सबसे अच्छा stage है। वजह याद रखिए — सबसे ज़्यादा condensed और सबसे कम overlapping, इसीलिए karyotyping इसी को इस्तेमाल करती है।

और उस जोड़ी की रखवाली कीजिए, क्योंकि paper उन्हें पास-पास रखना पसंद करता है। सबसे लंबा phase है interphase. Chromosomes study करने का सबसे अच्छा stage है metaphase. दो अलग सवाल, दो अलग जवाब, और दूसरे का criterion लंबाई नहीं — resolvability है।

sections.subtopic: Chapter Capstone: The Big Picture & Mitosis vs Meiosis
sections.title: Rapid revision II — the mitotic close and its significance

board_events.text: One-liners 6 to 8
6. Anaphase = centromeres split, sister chromatids $\to$ opposite poles.
7. Cytokinesis: animal = cleavage furrow (outside-in); plant = cell plate (inside-out); none $\Rightarrow$ syncytium (coconut).
Anchor the directions on the cell wall: a rigid wall cannot pinch, so the plant must BUILD outward.
8. Significance of mitosis: growth, repair/replacement, constant chromosome number, and cell-size control.
Cell-size control: a cell that grows too large has too much cytoplasm for one nucleus to service.
And remember the failure mode: mitosis escaping its check points is the basis of tumours and cancer.

segments.text: Second group. The end of mitosis, and what mitosis is for.
Six. Anaphase — the centromeres split, and the sister chromatids move to opposite poles. In mitosis. Hold that against anaphase one of meiosis, where they do not split.

Seven. Cytokinesis. Animal, cleavage furrow, working outside in. Plant, cell plate, working inside out. And if cytokinesis does not happen at all, you get a syncytium — the coconut's liquid endosperm.

And anchor those directions on the cell wall rather than memorising four things. A rigid wall cannot pinch, so the plant must build outward from the middle. An animal has no wall, so it can pinch inward. Get the constraint and both directions follow.

Eight. The significance of mitosis. Growth. Repair and replacement. Constant chromosome number. And cell size control — the nucleo cytoplasmic ratio. Four points, and the fourth is the one everybody forgets.

That fourth one is worth a sentence, since it is the one that gets dropped. A cell that grows too large has too much cytoplasm for a single nucleus to service. Dividing restores the balance. So mitosis is also a size regulator, not only a multiplier.

And remember the failure mode, because it is what makes the check points matter. Mitosis escaping its check points is uncontrolled proliferation — the basis of tumours and cancer. The same process that builds a body can dismantle it, and the only difference is regulation.
दूसरा group. Mitosis का अंत, और mitosis है किस लिए।
छह. Anaphase — centromeres split होते हैं, और sister chromatids उल्टे poles पर जाते हैं। Mitosis में। इसे meiosis के anaphase one से मिलाइए, जहाँ वो split नहीं होते।
सात. Cytokinesis. Animal, cleavage furrow, बाहर से अंदर। Plant, cell plate, अंदर से बाहर। और अगर cytokinesis होता ही नहीं, तो syncytium बनता है — नारियल का liquid endosperm.

और उन directions को चार चीज़ें रटने की जगह cell wall पर anchor कीजिए। Rigid wall pinch नहीं कर सकती, तो plant को बीच से बाहर की तरफ़ बनाना ही होगा। Animal के पास wall नहीं, तो वो अंदर की तरफ़ pinch कर सकता है। Constraint पकड़िए, दोनों directions निकल आएँगी।
आठ. Mitosis की significance. Growth. Repair और replacement. Constant chromosome number. और cell size control — nucleo cytoplasmic ratio. चार points, और चौथा वही है जो सब भूल जाते हैं।

चौथे पर एक वाक्य बनता है, क्योंकि वही छूटता है। जो cell बहुत बड़ा हो जाए, उसमें एक nucleus के संभालने के लिए cytoplasm ज़्यादा हो जाता है। Divide करना संतुलन लौटा देता है। तो mitosis सिर्फ़ multiplier नहीं, size regulator भी है।

और failure mode याद रखिए, क्योंकि उसी से check points मायने रखते हैं। Mitosis का अपने check points से बच निकलना uncontrolled proliferation है — tumours और cancer की बुनियाद। जो process शरीर बनाता है वही उसे तोड़ भी सकता है, और फ़र्क़ सिर्फ़ regulation का है।

sections.subtopic: Chapter Capstone: The Big Picture & Mitosis vs Meiosis
sections.title: Rapid revision III — meiosis

board_events.text: One-liners 9 to 12
9. Meiosis = two divisions, ONE replication $\to$ four haploid cells. Meiosis I reductional, Meiosis II equational.
10. Prophase I sub-stages: Leptotene $\to$ Zygotene (synapsis) $\to$ Pachytene (crossing over) $\to$ Diplotene (chiasmata) $\to$ Diakinesis (terminalization).
Each sub-stage is anchored to ONE signature event. Name an event, and you have named its sub-stage.
11. Anaphase I separates HOMOLOGUES (chromatids stay joined); Anaphase II separates SISTER CHROMATIDS.
12. Significance of meiosis: maintains chromosome-number constancy across generations + generates variation.
Both sources of variation are MEIOSIS I events. Meiosis II adds none.

segments.text: Third group. All of meiosis, in four lines.
Nine. Meiosis is two divisions and one replication, giving four haploid cells. Meiosis one reductional, Meiosis two equational. That single line contains most of two whole parts of this chapter.

Ten. The prophase one sub-stages. Leptotene, then zygotene which is synapsis, then pachytene which is crossing over, then diplotene which is chiasmata, then diakinesis which is terminalization. Late zebras play drums daily.

And that is not a list of five names — it is five name-and-event pairs. Each sub-stage is anchored to one signature event. So if a question names an event, it has already named its sub-stage, and you do not have to walk the list.
Eleven, and this is the line of the chapter. Anaphase one separates homologues, and the chromatids stay joined. Anaphase two separates sister chromatids. If you learn one one-liner, learn this one.

Twelve. The significance of meiosis. It maintains chromosome number constancy across generations, and it generates variation — through crossing over and independent assortment. That variation is the raw material of evolution.

And the detail inside point twelve that gets tested. Both sources of variation are Meiosis one events — crossing over in pachytene, independent assortment at metaphase one. Meiosis two adds none. So where does the variation among the four cells arise? Meiosis one. Every time.
तीसरा group. पूरा meiosis, चार lines में।
नौ. Meiosis यानी दो divisions और एक replication, जो चार haploid cells देते हैं। Meiosis one reductional, Meiosis two equational. यही एक line इस chapter के दो पूरे parts का ज़्यादातर हिस्सा समेटे है।

दस. Prophase one के sub-stages. Leptotene, फिर zygotene जो synapsis है, फिर pachytene जो crossing over है, फिर diplotene जो chiasmata है, फिर diakinesis जो terminalization है। Late zebras play drums daily.

और ये पाँच नामों की list नहीं है — ये नाम-और-event के पाँच जोड़े हैं। हर sub-stage एक signature event पर anchored है। तो अगर सवाल किसी event का नाम ले, तो उसने sub-stage का नाम ले ही लिया है, और आपको list पर चलना नहीं पड़ेगा।

ग्यारह, और यही इस chapter की line है। Anaphase one homologues को separate करता है, और chromatids जुड़े रहते हैं। Anaphase two sister chromatids को separate करता है। अगर एक ही one-liner सीखनी हो, तो यही सीखिए।

बारह. Meiosis की significance. वो generations के आर-पार chromosome number की constancy बनाए रखता है, और variation पैदा करता है — crossing over और independent assortment से। वही variation evolution का कच्चा माल है।

और point बारह के अंदर वो detail जो जाँची जाती है। Variation के दोनों sources Meiosis one के events हैं — pachytene में crossing over, metaphase one पर independent assortment. Meiosis two कुछ नहीं जोड़ता। तो चारों cells में variation कहाँ पैदा होती है? Meiosis one. हर बार।

board_events.text: THREE DIVISIONS TO KNOW: Mitosis (equational, somatic); Meiosis I (reductional); Meiosis II (equational).
COUNTING RULES: n mitotic divisions $\to 2^n$ cells; one meiosis $\to$ 4 haploid cells; meiocytes needed = cells $\div$ 4.
DNA / NUMBER PATH (meiosis): $G_2$: 4C / 2n $\to$ after Meiosis I: 2C / n $\to$ after Meiosis II: 1C / n.
LIFE CYCLE: meiosis HALVES ($2n \to n$), fertilisation RESTORES ($n + n \to 2n$), mitosis MULTIPLIES.
THE BIG CONTRAST: mitosis = identical diploid copies; meiosis = varied haploid cells (synapsis + crossing over + independent assortment).
MEMORY AIDS: mitotic stages 'PMAT'; Meiosis-I sub-stages 'L-Z-P-D-D'.
CHAPTER MOTTO: meiosis halves, fertilisation restores, mitosis multiplies.

segments.text: And now the whole chapter on one page. This is the last thing to read before you walk into the exam.
Six panels. Read them in order and you have traversed everything we have done across four parts.
Three divisions to know. Mitosis — equational, somatic. Meiosis one — reductional. Meiosis two — equational. Two of the three are equational, and only one reduces. That asymmetry is the chapter.

Counting rules. n mitotic divisions give two to the power n cells. One meiosis gives four haploid cells. And meiocytes needed equals cells divided by four. Two rules, and the skill is picking the right one.

The D N A and number path through meiosis. G two, four C and two n. After Meiosis one, two C and n. After Meiosis two, one C and n. Watch which one moves at each arrow — the number moves once, the D N A moves twice.
The life cycle. Meiosis halves, two n to n. Fertilisation restores, n plus n to two n. Mitosis multiplies. Three arrows, one circle, and every stage in this chapter sits somewhere on it.

The big contrast. Mitosis gives identical diploid copies. Meiosis gives varied haploid cells — and the variety comes from three things, synapsis, crossing over, and independent assortment. Mitosis copies; meiosis halves and shuffles.
The memory aids. P M A T for the mitotic stages — please make a two. And L Z P D D for the Meiosis one sub-stages — late zebras play drums daily. Two phrases that between them order nine stages.

And if everything else goes, keep the chapter motto. Meiosis halves, fertilisation restores, mitosis multiplies. Seven words. From them you can rebuild the life cycle, and from the life cycle you can place every stage, every count, and every division in this chapter. That is the whole of cell cycle and cell division.
और अब पूरा chapter एक page पर। Exam में जाने से पहले आख़िरी चीज़ जो पढ़नी है, यही है।
छह panels. इन्हें क्रम से पढ़िए और आप वो सब पार कर चुके जो हमने चार parts में किया।
तीन divisions जानने हैं। Mitosis — equational, somatic. Meiosis one — reductional. Meiosis two — equational. तीन में से दो equational हैं, और सिर्फ़ एक reduce करता है। यही asymmetry पूरा chapter है।
Counting rules. n mitotic divisions देते हैं two to the power n cells. एक meiosis देता है चार haploid cells. और meiocytes चाहिए बराबर cells divided by four. दो rules, और skill है सही वाला चुनना।
Meiosis में D N A और number का रास्ता। G two, four C और two n. Meiosis one के बाद, two C और n. Meiosis two के बाद, one C और n. हर arrow पर देखिए क्या हिलता है — number एक बार हिलता है, D N A दो बार।
Life cycle. Meiosis halves, two n से n. Fertilisation restores, n plus n से two n. Mitosis multiplies. तीन arrows, एक घेरा, और इस chapter का हर stage उसी पर कहीं बैठा है।

बड़ा contrast. Mitosis identical diploid copies देता है। Meiosis varied haploid cells देता है — और वो variety तीन चीज़ों से आती है, synapsis, crossing over, और independent assortment. Mitosis copies; meiosis halves and shuffles.
Memory aids. Mitotic stages के लिए P M A T — please make a two. और Meiosis one के sub-stages के लिए L Z P D D — late zebras play drums daily. दो वाक्यांश, जो मिलकर नौ stages को क्रम में रख देते हैं।

और अगर बाक़ी सब चला जाए, तो chapter का motto पकड़े रहिए। Meiosis halves, fertilisation restores, mitosis multiplies. सात शब्द। इनसे आप life cycle दोबारा बना सकते हैं, और life cycle से इस chapter का हर stage, हर गिनती, और हर division अपनी जगह रख सकते हैं। यही पूरा cell cycle and cell division है।
